success_criteria:
  - "resolveDaemonOwnerKeyID distinguishes 'not configured' (absent daemon.json -- unchanged behavior, verification skipped) from 'configured but unresolvable' (present daemon.json that fails to resolve an owner key -- command loading must be disabled entirely, never fall through to loading commands unverified). The call site in main.go's runCmd must not invoke daemon.LoadCommands at all when enforcement was requested but could not be resolved; commands must be an empty map in that case."
  - "LoadCommands/loadCommand take a *slog.Logger parameter (nil falls back to slog.Default(), so existing test call sites using the package-level slog.SetDefault/installCapturingHandler pattern keep working) and main.go passes its own configured daemon logger, so the 'reject command file: signature verification failed' Error line reaches the daemon's log file (~/.punt-labs/beadle/logs/beadle-daemon.log), not just stderr."
  - "LoadCommands distinguishes three outcomes for a failed loadCommand call, not two: a *SignatureError (existing Error-level 'reject command file: signature verification failed' with reason/detail), an operational verification failure that occurred while ownerKeyID != '' (a new, distinctly-named Error-level log line -- verification infrastructure broke while enforcement was active, not a parse error), and everything else (existing Warn-level 'skip invalid command file'). ownerKeyID is already in LoadCommands' scope."
  - "internal/daemon/config.go's Config struct doc comment states the OwnerHandle/OwnerGPGKeyID mutual-exclusivity invariant and that a freshly-parsed Config is not yet validated until ResolveOwnerKeyID runs."
  - "main.go's startup log line for commands loaded reports whether signature enforcement is active (ownerKeyID != \"\"), not just the count."
  - "New tests cover: a present-but-misconfigured daemon.json (ambiguous, unresolvable handle, malformed fingerprint) results in zero commands loaded and LoadCommands is never called; a rejected command file's Error log is observable through a logger passed into LoadCommands, not just the package default; an operational VerifySignature failure (e.g. gpg binary that cannot run) while ownerKeyID != \"\" produces the new distinct Error log, not the generic Warn."
  - "make check passes with zero suppressions."
  - "Commit incrementally -- one commit per logical step (file group, single concern, or single PR-equivalent slice). Each commit must pass make check. Do not accumulate more than 30 minutes of uncommitted changes."
context: |
  Three async local-review agents (code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter,
  type-design-analyzer) ran on the full diff of feat/wire-verifysignature
  vs main in <repo>, per WORKFLOW.md Phase 5,
  before this branch's PR opens. Findings:

  1. CRITICAL (code-reviewer, confidence 92): cmd/beadle-daemon/main.go's
     resolveDaemonOwnerKeyID returns "" on every resolution failure --
     absent daemon.json (correct, unconfigured) AND present-but-broken
     daemon.json (wrong). "" then flows straight into
     daemon.LoadCommands(cmdDir, gpgBinary, ""), and internal/daemon/command.go's
     loadCommand gates VerifySignature on ownerKeyID != "" -- so a
     misconfigured daemon.json does not disable command loading, it disables
     *verification* while still loading every command file unsigned. This is
     the exact always-authorize backdoor DES-034/DES-035 exist to close, and
     it hits precisely the operators who opted in and typo'd something.
     docs/wire-verifysignature.md's own prose (line ~141-144) already states
     the required behavior: "must never silently mean 'skip verification'".
     The fix must separate "never opted in" (verification skipped, unchanged
     legacy behavior) from "opted in and it didn't take effect" (command
     loading disabled entirely -- LoadCommands must not run).

  2. IMPORTANT (code-reviewer, confidence 85): LoadCommands logs signature
     rejections via package-level slog.Error/slog.Warn (slog.Default()).
     main.go never calls slog.SetDefault -- it builds its own logger and
     threads it explicitly everywhere else (PipelineStore.Logger,
     WorkerSpawner.Logger, NewMailHandler, NewPoller). LoadCommands is the
     one call that doesn't take a logger, so the highest-value audit event
     this feature produces -- a rejected, tampered, or wrong-key command
     file -- never reaches ~/.punt-labs/beadle/logs/beadle-daemon.log, only
     bare stderr. docs/wire-verifysignature.md's fail-soft rationale
     explicitly depends on this log persisting ("you'll notice no commands
     run and the log names why").

  3. (silent-failure-hunter): VerifySignature can fail two structurally
     different ways: a genuine signature verdict (*SignatureError,
     internal/daemon/signature.go) or an operational failure inside the
     verification pipeline itself (gpg binary missing/unusable, temp dir
     creation failing, etc. -- returned as a plain wrapped error). loadCommand
     wraps either kind identically; LoadCommands' errors.As(err, &sigErr)
     only catches the first kind, so an operational failure (verification
     infrastructure broken while enforcement is actively configured) falls
     into the same generic Warn-level "skip invalid command file" as a YAML
     typo -- indistinguishable, and invisible to an operator grepping for the
     Error-level rejection line docs/wire-verifysignature.md names as the
     alerting surface. Recommendation in the finding: a distinct Error-level
     log line for this case (ownerKeyID != "" is already in scope in
     LoadCommands).

  4. (type-design-analyzer, cheap): internal/daemon/Config's struct doc
     comment doesn't state that OwnerHandle/OwnerGPGKeyID are mutually
     exclusive or that a freshly-parsed Config isn't yet validated --
     one-comment fix, no behavior change. (The other two
     type-design-analyzer suggestions -- a LoadConfig test for the
     both-fields-set case, and NOT adding a constructor/private fields --
     are optional/already-decided; do not action them beyond the doc
     comment.)

  The leader made a direct one-line edit to config.go's doc comment (finding
  4) before catching that this violates the "leader does not write
  production code" rule and reverted it -- do that fix as part of this
  mission instead, alongside the other three.

  Read docs/wire-verifysignature.md (DES-035) end to end first for the full
  design context -- particularly the fail-soft rationale in the section that
  discusses why a misconfiguration disables command loading rather than the
  whole daemon (mail polling and the MCP server have no dependency on the
  commands map -- that property must NOT change).
budget:
  rounds: 3
  reflection_after_each: true
